_source: WHO CVD Risk Charts 2019 (SEAR-B) · NICE NG238 2023 · ESC/EAS 2021 · ISH Global 2020
_context: Sri Lanka / South Asian. 10-year risk. NO Australian guidelines used.

LOW.management: Lifestyle advice. No pharmacotherapy for primary prevention.

MODERATE.management: Lifestyle intensive. Consider statin if risk factors persist.

VERY HIGH.management: High-intensity statin (atorvastatin 40–80mg). BP ≤130/80. Aspirin not routine in primary prevention.

nice_ng238_statin_threshold.note: ≥40% non-HDL reduction target at 3 months. If not achieved: titrate up or add ezetimibe.

clinical_high_risk_bypass: Established CVD (prior MI, angina, stroke/TIA, PCI/CABG, PVD, aortic aneurysm)
Diabetes mellitus with end-organ damage (nephropathy, retinopathy, neuropathy, microalbuminuria)
Markedly elevated single risk factor: SBP ≥180 mmHg or TC ≥8.0 mmol/L

triglyceride_thresholds.note: TG >11.3 mmol/L = pancreatitis emergency. TG >5.6 mmol/L = consider fenofibrate.

south_asian_risk_modifiers.evidence: Tillin 2013 (SABRE cohort); INTERHEART South Asia; WHO SEAR-B calibration
south_asian_risk_modifiers.note: South Asians develop CVD at younger age and lower traditional risk factor burden. 1.4× multiplier applied to all WHO SEAR-B calculated risks.

reclassification_factors_upward: Family history premature CVD (1st-degree: male <55, female <65)
High hsCRP (>2.0 mg/L) — independent inflammatory marker
Moderate CKD (eGFR 30–59 mL/min) — independent CVD risk
Central obesity: waist >90cm (M) / >80cm (F) — South Asian thresholds

reassessment_frequency.on_pharmacotherapy: Every 3 months until stable, then annually

cha2ds2vasc.alternative: Warfarin if NOAC contraindicated or unavailable
